title: RISC-V Vectorization Coverage for HPC: A TSVC-Based Analysis
problem: RISC-V Vector Extension (RVV) has potential for HPC but compiler auto-vectorization support unclear; unknown instruction coverage and missed optimization opportunities
motivation: Evaluate current compiler support for RVV vectorization to guide future compiler development and identify barriers to HPC adoption
method: The researchers compiled HPC benchmark programs using two major compilers—GNU and LLVM—testing both variable-length vector mode (VLA, where width adapts) and fixed-length vector mode (VLS, where width is fixed). They measured which vectorization instructions each compiler actually generated and categorized all vectorization failures into three types: compiler backend limitations, missed optimization opportunities (patterns the compiler doesn't recognize), and unsupported instruction patterns.
key_novelty: This work comprehensively analyzes which RISC-V vector instructions GNU and LLVM compilers actually generate when vectorizing HPC workloads.
contributions: Comparison of GNU and LLVM compiler support
Identification of missed instructions and optimization opportunities
limitations: Analysis limited to TSVC benchmark kernels; may not reflect all HPC patterns; specific coverage percentages not in abstract
